body:
## Issue #27867

SUMMARIZE over the nanosecond temporal types added in 2.0 raised a binder error:



SUMMARIZE generates \x60avg()\x60 and \x60approx_quantile(x, pos)\x60 for temporal columns, but neither function had overloads for \x60TIMESTAMP_NS\x60, \x60TIMESTAMPTZ_NS\x60 or \x60TIME_NS\x60.

## Root cause

- \x60avg\x60: no overloads for the three \x60_NS\x60 temporal types. \x60TIMESTAMP_NS\x60 only worked at all via a lossy implicit cast to \x60TIMESTAMP\x60 (nanoseconds truncated to microseconds); \x60TIMESTAMPTZ_NS\x60 and \x60TIME_NS\x60 did not bind at all.
- \x60approx_quantile\x60: the \x60INT64\x60 internal-type dispatch path already handled these types, but they were never registered.

## Fix

- **avg.cpp**: add native \x60avg()\x60 overloads for \x60TIMESTAMP_NS\x60, \x60TIMESTAMPTZ_NS\x60 and \x60TIME_NS\x60 using \x60DiscreteAverageOperation\x60 (the same integer-rounding path as \x60TIME\x60/\x60TIMESTAMP\x60), preserving nanosecond precision. \x60TIME_NS\x60 gets a nanosecond state-import validator mirroring the existing microsecond \x60ValidateTimeAverageStates\x60.
- **approximate_quantile.cpp**: register the three \x60_NS\x60 temporal types for \x60approx_quantile(x, FLOAT)\x60 (the single-arg form SUMMARIZE uses).

## Verification

- New regression test \x60test/sql/show_select/test_summarize_temporal_ns.test\x60 (8 assertions) — passes.
- Existing suites all green: \x60test/sql/aggregate/*\x60 (232 cases, 258345 assertions), \x60*quantile*\x60 (24 cases), \x60*summarize*\x60 (6), \x60[show_select]\x60 (14), \x60temporal_avg.fuzz\60, \x60test_time_ns.test\x60.

Note: \x60approx_quantile\x60 over \x60_NS\x60 types returns values with sub-second precision limited by the 53-bit HLL sketch (pre-existing property of the approximate function) — SUMMARIZE only requires it to bind and return the correct type, which this provides. \x60avg\x60 is exact.

Fixes #27867

The only failure in this run is `test/sql/storage/reclaim_space/test_reclaim_space_update_large_string.test` under `Linux Config (Persistence)` (config `force_storage_restart.json`). It fails right after a `restart` with `Catalog Error: Table with name test does not exist` — i.e. the table was not recovered from storage. This is a storage/WAL-recovery path that is not touched by this PR (which only adds avg/approx_quantile overloads for nanosecond temporal types in `avg.cpp` / `approximate_quantile.cpp`). The test passes locally on the exact commit (60 assertions, all green), including under repeated runs; the failure is a CI-environment flake that also failed all 4 CI retries (consistent with a transient runner state issue). Re-triggering CI.

Re-running: the only failure in this run (40731649872) is `regression / Bench IMDB`, which failed with `The self-hosted runner lost communication with the server` — a self-hosted runner disconnection (infrastructure), not a test failure or code issue. The previous run's single failure (the `reclaim_space` storage-restart test) did not recur. All functional test jobs — including every avg/temporal/timestamp/date regression — pass in both runs.

### What happens?

I have upgraded from 1.5.x to 2.0 today and discovered that the SUMMARIZE statement caused an error when detecting TIMESTAMPTZ_NS column types

`SUMMARIZE SELECT
    TIMESTAMPTZ_NS '2026-10-26 09:30:15.123456789+10:00' AS ts_ns;
`

with 

_SQL Error: Binder Error: No function matches the given name and argument types 'avg(TIMESTAMPTZ_NS)'. You might need to add explicit type casts.
	Candidate functions:
	avg(x DECIMAL) -> DECIMAL
	avg(x SMALLINT, /) -> DOUBLE
	avg(x INTEGER, /) -> DOUBLE
	avg(x BIGINT, /) -> DOUBLE
	avg(x HUGEINT, /) -> DOUBLE
	avg(x INTERVAL, /) -> INTERVAL
	avg(x DOUBLE, /) -> DOUBLE
	avg(x TIMESTAMP, /) -> TIMESTAMP
	avg(x TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, /) -> TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
	avg(x TIME, /) -> TIME
	avg(x TIME WITH TIME ZONE, /) -> TIME WITH TIME ZONE_





### To Reproduce

SUMMARIZE SELECT
    TIMESTAMPTZ_NS '2026-10-26 09:30:15.123456789+10:00' AS ts_ns;
